creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Editing a card with both a title and an invalid custom field value applies the title anyway:

    kan edit <card> -t "MUTATED" -f type=bogus
    -> exit 1, stderr: invalid type: must be one of: feature, enhancement, bug, chore, ...
    -> but the card is now titled "MUTATED", with type left unset

So the card ends up renamed, the field unset, and an error printed - the worst of the three possible outcomes, and the one hardest to notice. Reproduced on board/12 against a wanted enum field.

Why this matters beyond the typo case: it makes edit unsafe for any script or hook that sets a field and a title in one call. The type-shortcut pattern hook shipped in the Claude skill now has to fetch board describe --json and validate the type itself before it dares call edit - purely so that a title like "Fix the important override" (with a bang in front of "important") does not get silently renamed when the bang turns out not to name a real type. That is an extra CLI round-trip on every hook invocation, existing only to work around this.

If a failed edit left the card untouched, that validation step and its cost would disappear, and callers could treat a nonzero exit as "nothing happened".

Open question whether the right shape is validating every input before applying any of them, or applying and rolling back on failure.
title: Failed edit still applies the title change
